Discovering that trust may have been manufactured rather than earned was humiliating and unsettling, particularly for anyone seeking help during a vulnerable time.Mental health services demand honesty, transparency, and integrity. Using misleading marketing strategies and fabricated or manipulated reviews in this space is not just unfair trade practice—it is ethically unacceptable. People come to such services looking for real support, not sales funnels disguised as care.I want to be clear: this review is not written out of anger, but out of disgust and firm rejection of these practices. I strongly caution others to do their own independent research, look beyond surface-level reviews, and question overly polished narratives before engaging with any service that claims to offer care or support. I have proofs of their lead generation through paid reviews and funnel spamming.
